title: Dharma Field Extractor Turns Any Document Into JSON
summary: Dharma AI launches Field Extractor, an open-source tool that converts unstructured documents into structured JSON output with user-defined schemas.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Dharma AI released Field Extractor, an open-source tool that extracts structured data from any document format into JSON.
- The system supports custom schemas, handles PDFs, images, and text with near-instant processing speeds.
- Available now on Hugging Face with Apache 2.0 licensing for commercial and research applications.


Dharma AI has launched Field Extractor, an open-source tool that converts unstructured documents into structured JSON output with user-defined schemas. Released on Hugging Face on November 4, 2026, the system processes PDFs, images, and text files to extract specific fields without requiring manual data entry or complex parsing rules.


## How Field Extractor Works


The tool accepts documents in multiple formats and a schema definition specifying the fields to extract. Users provide a JSON template describing the desired output structure, including field names, types, and optional validation rules. Field Extractor analyzes the document content and returns a JSON object matching the schema. The system handles variations in document layout, formatting inconsistencies, and multiple languages without requiring document-specific training.


Processing speeds average under two seconds per page for standard business documents. The model supports nested JSON structures, allowing extraction of complex hierarchical data like invoice line items, table rows, or multi-level organization charts.


## Technical Architecture and Performance


Field Extractor combines vision-language models with structured output generation to maintain accuracy across document types. The system uses[document understanding](https://emergent.sh/glossary/document-understanding) techniques to identify key-value pairs, tables, and text blocks regardless of their position on the page. Dharma AI reports 94% accuracy on standard benchmark datasets for invoice, receipt, and form extraction tasks.


- Supports PDF, PNG, JPG, TIFF, and plain text inputs
- Handles documents up to 50 pages in a single request
- Returns JSON output with confidence scores for each extracted field
- Provides fallback values and error handling for missing or ambiguous data


## Release Date and Availability


Field Extractor was officially launched on November 4, 2026, through the Hugging Face model hub. The tool is available under an Apache 2.0 license, permitting commercial use, modification, and redistribution. Dharma AI provides Python and REST API interfaces for integration into existing workflows.


The release includes pre-built connectors for common[document automation](https://emergent.sh/glossary/document-automation) pipelines and examples for invoice processing, contract analysis, and form digitization. Developers can deploy the model on local infrastructure or use Hugging Face's hosted inference endpoints for production workloads.


## Use Cases and Applications


Organizations can apply Field Extractor to automate data entry from invoices, purchase orders, contracts, medical records, and insurance claims. The system replaces manual keying workflows that introduce errors and slow processing times. Financial services firms use the tool to extract transaction details from bank statements, while healthcare providers digitize patient intake forms and lab reports.


The open-source nature allows customization for domain-specific document types. Teams can fine-tune the base model on proprietary document sets to improve accuracy for specialized formats like scientific papers, legal filings, or technical specifications.


## What This Means


Dharma AI's Field Extractor lowers the barrier for organizations to implement document processing automation without vendor lock-in or per-page pricing. The Apache 2.0 license and Hugging Face distribution enable rapid prototyping and production deployment. As unstructured data volumes grow across industries, tools that reliably convert documents into structured formats become critical infrastructure for AI-driven workflows.
